title: AI capability · hancrafted
description: An interactive timeline of four Levels of working with AI, from chat to the emerging factory, with the effort each asks you to manage, its productivity increase against what studies measured, how many people work at it, the AI disciplines it adds, and where a person sits in the loop.

slides.text: “20× productivity with AI.” Here’s what that actually means. Explore four Levels of working with AI on one timeline, and what each one adds. Try it Why it matters Show it to your team Settle the vocabulary in one meeting: press Play all and let the timeline do the talking. Copy link AI capability 2022–2026 2022–23 Chat like a task 2024–25 Agents like a specialist 2024–25 Workflows like a team 2026 → Factory like an organisation Language model predicts the next token

The timeline Four Levels on one language model, from chat in 2022–23 to the factory emerging in 2026. Explain Managing effort Productivity increase Adoption AI disciplines Oversight ▶ Play all 2022–23 Chat You write, the AI answers. The entry point. Click: definition Definition : Chat is a conversation with the model: you write instructions, it answers, message by message. Source : OpenAI, prompt engineering guide ↗ ( opens in a new tab ) Summarise this report in 3 points. Sure: 1. … 2. … 3. … Chat a conversation: you write, it answers, message by message 2024–25 Agents The AI uses tools and works in a loop. Click: definition Definition : An agent is a language model that uses tools in a loop and decides for itself how to reach a goal. Source : Anthropic, Building effective agents (2024) ↗ ( opens in a new tab ) done Plan the team's trip to the trade fair. Open the web Search flights Three options, cheapest first. Harness the software around it: permissions, tools and a loop until done 2024–26 Workflows Several agents, step by step, to a plan. Click: definition Definition : A workflow chains model and tool steps along a path fixed in advance. Source : Anthropic, Building effective agents (2024) ↗ ( opens in a new tab ) Flowchart a graph of agents with a human in or on the loop 2026 → · emerging Factory? Agents run the lifecycle, spec to release. People pass the gates. Click: definition Definition : A factory runs the whole development lifecycle with agents, from specification to release; people set the goals and pass its gates. Source : Shapiro, The Five Levels (2026) ↗ ( opens in a new tab ) ? Lifecycle requests in, agents at every stage, people at the gates ‹ › Large language model (LLM) The foundation, under every stage It predicts, token A token is a piece of a word, such as "special" + "ist". Models read and write text in tokens. by token, which word piece most likely comes next, learnt from vast amounts of training text. ChatGPT, Copilot, Claude. Click: definition New tech nology brings ? Definition : A large language model is an AI model trained on vast amounts of text that continues text token by token and is steered by text alone. Source : Brown et al. 2020, Language Models are Few-Shot Learners ↗ ( opens in a new tab ) Read me timeline What it shows Four Levels on one language model, each with its card, a scene and its wire down to the model. Explain is on; the toolbar adds rows that tell the same timeline from other angles: the effort each Level asks you to manage, its productivity increase, how many people work at it, the AI disciplines it adds, and where a person sits in its oversight. What to try Switch on AI disciplines, then Oversight. Click a card to open the definitions behind it, each from the page that gives it. Move the mouse onto a Level to play its scene; click a Level card or the model band for its definition. On a phone, swipe from Level to Level. What to notice The productivity increases are hypotheses; the measured line under each says what studies found, and no study has measured a workflow or a factory yet. Each adoption number counts a different population, so the four do not add up to one curve. Every discipline stays once added: a factory still needs prompts.

Why · How · What Prompt, agent, workflow, factory: four words that get mixed up, on one timeline. Why Everyone says agent and workflow, and nobody says what differs. The words fly around, and "factory" has no settled definition at all. ( ) So it is hard to know which one you need. Even “20x productivity” is an estimate, not a measurement. ( ) How Each layer adds one thing to the same model. A chat is you writing instructions and the model answering; an agent directs its own tool use in a loop; a workflow chains steps along a path fixed in advance. ( ) What Four Levels on one timeline, from 2022 to 2026. ChatGPT launched in November 2022, agents and workflows were defined in December 2024, and the factory emerged in early 2026. ( ) Play each scene or press "Play all".

Play Where the years and definitions come from Every year, definition and source on the cards comes from research LLM-0018, which dates each discipline by its primary source: ChatGPT's launch for chat, Anthropic's agent definition and Claude Code for agents, LangGraph for workflows, and Dan Shapiro's five levels and StrongDM for the factory. The measured productivity comes from research LLM-0019, the adoption numbers from LLM-0025, the AI disciplines from LLM-0023 and the oversight modes from LLM-0024. Where in, on and out of the loop come from The three oversight terms come from the debate on weapon autonomy, not from software. Human Rights Watch and Harvard's International Human Rights Clinic set them out in Losing Humanity (2012): human-in-the-loop weapons select and engage targets only with a human command; human-on-the-loop weapons do so under a human operator who can override their actions; human-out-of-the-loop weapons do so without any human input or interaction. Where each mode sits on the timeline is a hypothesis (research LLM-0024).

About Where “20x” comes from Marc Andreessen says leading-edge programmers at a16z portfolio companies are “like 20x more productive than they were a year ago”, an estimate by an investor with no method given 1 . A randomized trial measured experienced developers 19% slower with AI 2 (research AIE-0017). Sources (2) a16z Show, Marc Andreessen on Builder Culture in the Age of AI ( opens in a new tab ) a16z.com Becker et al., Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org The words are not settled Chat, agents and workflows have first-party definitions, but "factory" is a 2026 practitioner label 1 , and its definitions differ in how much human review remains 2 (research LLM-0018). Sources (2) StrongDM, The Software Factory ( opens in a new tab ) factory.strongdm.ai Grant, Dark Factories: Agentic Software Factories (briefing, secondary) ( opens in a new tab ) chadgrant.github.io Three first-party definitions OpenAI defines prompt engineering as writing effective instructions for a model 1 . Anthropic calls workflows systems where LLMs and tools follow predefined code paths, and agents systems where LLMs direct their own tool use 2 . Willison settles on an agent as an LLM that runs tools in a loop to achieve a goal 3 (research LLM-0018). Sources (3) OpenAI, Prompt engineering guide ( opens in a new tab ) developers.openai.com Anthropic, Building effective agents ( opens in a new tab ) anthropic.com Willison, I think "agent" may finally have a widely enough agreed upon definition ( opens in a new tab ) simonwillison.net Dates from primary sources ChatGPT launched on 30 November 2022 1 ; Anthropic defined agents and workflows on 19 December 2024 2 ; the factory label dates from early 2026, and the practice began in mid-2025 at one team 3 (research LLM-0018). Sources (3) OpenAI, Introducing ChatGPT ( opens in a new tab ) openai.com Anthropic, Building effective agents ( opens in a new tab ) anthropic.com StrongDM, The Software Factory ( opens in a new tab ) factory.strongdm.ai
